 The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender

entities.text: Vanaparla Lingaiah 2 Others vs B. Praveen Kumar And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
:
Aggrieved by the award dated 14.06.2011 in O.P.No.444 of 2008 passed by the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum- Special Sessions Judge for trial of SCs/STs (POA) Cases-cum-Addl.
District Judge, Nalgonda, the claimants have filed MACMA No.1903 of 2011 for enhancement of the compensation while Insurance Company has filed MACMA No.4399 of 2012 questioning the quantum of compensation.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum- Special Sessions Judge
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Since both the appeals arise out of the very same finding in O.P.No.444 of 2008, both the appeals are disposed of by way of common judgment.

3. Heard both sides and perused the entire material on record.
4.
The claim petition was filed claiming compensation of Rs.12,00,000/- on the death of the deceased in the motor vehicle accident.
On the basis of the claim petition filed, the trial Court having considered the evidence on record granted compensation of Rs.6,40,000/- to be paid to the claimants.
6. The manner in which the accident has taken place is not in dispute.
Further, it is not in dispute regarding insurer of the offending vehicle.

7. The main contention of the learned counsel for the Insurance company is that in accordance with the Schedule-II of the M.V.Act, any compensation under Section 163-A cannot exceed Rs.5.00Lakhs.
8.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the claimants would submit that the Schedule-II of the M.V.Act came into existence in the year 1994 and there is an amending inflation but the Schedule was not reconsidered.

In the similar circumstances, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kurvan Ansari v.
Shyam Kishore Murmu 1 considered the quantum over and above the amount mentioned in the Schedule.

entities.text:
Kurvan Ansari v.
Shyam Kishore Murmu 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. It is a fact that the inflation has gone up considerably after 1994.
However, no steps are taken to modify or reconsider the values in Schedule-II of the Act.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I do not find any infirmity in the finding of the Tribunal and following the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kurvan Ansari case (supra)., the appeals are liable to be dismissed.
11. The Tribunal granted an amount of Rs.6,24,000/- towards loss of dependency and the said finding remains unaltered.
12. The Tribunal has granted meager amounts under the other heads.

As regards the consortium to be paid, claimant Nos.1 and 2 are entitled to Rs.40,000/- each towards consortium as decided by the Hon'ble Apex court in case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi 2.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi 2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Claimant No.3 is granted an amount of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of love and affection.

With regard to the funeral expenses and loss of estate, the claimants are entitled for Rs.30,000/-.
13.

In the light of the above discussion, the claimants are entitled for the following compensation under different heads:
 Head Compensation awarded  (1) Loss of dependency Rs.6,24,000  (2) Loss of love and affection Rs.40,000  2017 (6) 170 (SC)
 KS, J  MACMA_1903_2011 and  4399_2012  (3) Funeral expenses and Loss of Estate Rs.30,000  (4) Filial consortium Rs.80,000

Total compensation awarded Rs.7,74,000/-
14.

In the result, the MACMA No.4399 of 2012 is dismissed and MACMA No.1903 of 2011 is partly allowed enhancing the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal from Rs.6,40,600/- to Rs.7,74,000/- as hereunder:
(a) The enhanced amount shall carry interest at 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization.
(b) The respondent No.2 shall deposit the amount within a period of (8) weeks from the date of receipt of copy of judgment.

On such deposit, claimants are entitled to Vanaparla Lingaiah 2 Others vs B. Praveen Kumar And Another on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64525805/
2 withdraw the entire amount without furnishing the security.

Total compensation awarded Rs.7,74,000/-
